# Contact Relationship Management

A central hub for managing interactions with customers and prospects across
the relationship lifecycle: sales automation, marketing automation, customer
support, and analytics.

> ⚠️ **Not ready for production.** The data is synthetic, and no real email
> is sent unless a real mail mode is configured. See the
> [path to production](locales/en-us/path-to-production/index.md) for what
> production means here and an estimate of how far each part has got, and
> [spec/regulatory.md](spec/regulatory.md).

## Contents

- [contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust](contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust/) —
  JSON API in Rust on Axum and axa (PostgreSQL through sqlx).
- [contact-relationship-management-matcher-with-rust](contact-relationship-management-matcher-with-rust/) —
  library: the probability that two contact records are the same person.
- [contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte](contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte/) —
  Svelte client for sales, marketing, and support.
- [contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-swift](contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-swift/) —
  iOS app (SwiftUI, Lily Design System for Swift) for a rep or agent away from a desk.
- [contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-kotlin](contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-kotlin/) —
  Android app (Jetpack Compose, Lily Design System for Kotlin), the same screens.
- [spec](spec/index.md) — the cross-cutting specification, the single source
  of truth for both editions.
- [contact-relationship-management.github.io](contact-relationship-management.github.io/README.md) —
  the documentation site for GitHub Pages (static SvelteKit), published at
  <https://contact-relationship-management.github.io/>.
- [docs](docs/) — tutorials and reference material:
  [the family bridges](docs/tutorial-family-bridges.md) (the project portfolio
  and worker services, signed WPM events, the employment check), and the NHS
  [DTAC 2.0](docs/united-kingdom/national-health-service/digital-technology-assessment-criteria/2.0/index.md)
  notes.

## Quick start

See [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). In short: `cd
contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte && pnpm install && pnpm dev`,
then sign in as `example@example.com` for a guided tour on fictitious data, with
no service needed.

## GitHub Pages site

[contact-relationship-management.github.io/](contact-relationship-management.github.io/README.md)
is a static site of this README, INSTALL, the family-bridges tutorial, the
specification index, the locale status and the role briefs in all 16 locales
(Arabic right to left), with a landing page, a tutorial and comparison pages,
published at <https://contact-relationship-management.github.io/>. It is built and tested here
(`scripts/ci-check.sh site`) and exported to the read-only repository
`contact-relationship-management/contact-relationship-management.github.io`,
which deploys it with GitHub Actions.

To publish a change, from a clone with the `github-pages` remote:

1. After editing any document the site shows, run `pnpm run sync` in the site's
   directory (CI fails on a stale copy).
2. Commit, then run `make publish-github-pages` from the repository root. That runs
   `bin/publish-github-pages`, which checks the remote, the site's copy of the
   documents and a clean directory, then runs
   `git subtree push --prefix=contact-relationship-management.github.io github-pages main`.
3. Watch the deploy run in the exported repository.

The remote lives in each clone, so a new clone adds it once:
`git remote add github-pages git@github.com:contact-relationship-management/contact-relationship-management.github.io.git`

Never work in the exported repository. See
[spec/github-pages-site.md](spec/github-pages-site.md).

## Works on its own

This repository builds, runs and is tested **without** the project-portfolio (PPM) or workforce-planning (WPM)
repositories: nothing here depends on their code. The bridges are opt-in and off until configured
(`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PPM_SERVICE_URL`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_URL`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)); the inbound
webhook answers `404` while its secret is unset. A bridge carries references and counts, never a record.
Walk-through: [docs/tutorial-family-bridges.md](docs/tutorial-family-bridges.md).

## Documents

[INSTALL](INSTALL.md) · [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [RFC](RFC.md) ·
[NEWS](NEWS.md) · [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) · [COMPARISONS](COMPARISONS.md) ·
[BENCHMARKS](BENCHMARKS.md) · [GOVERNANCE](GOVERNANCE.md) ·
[MAINTAINERS](MAINTAINERS.md) · [SECURITY](SECURITY.md) ·
[AI_STATEMENT](AI_STATEMENT.md) · [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) ·
[LICENSE](LICENSE.md)

## Contact

# Comparisons

How this project relates to other CRM software. This is a demonstration
project, not a competitor to mature products.

| Project                                      | Kind                         | Relationship                                                       |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [Twenty](https://twenty.com)                 | Open-source CRM              | Full product; this project is a smaller, spec-driven demo          |
| [EspoCRM](https://www.espocrm.com)           | Open-source CRM (PHP)        | Broader features; this project emphasizes explainable rules        |
| [SuiteCRM](https://suitecrm.com)             | Open-source CRM (PHP)        | Mature, large; this project is a compact reference                 |
| Salesforce, HubSpot                          | Commercial SaaS CRM          | The practice this project models; no code or data is shared        |

## Side by side

Each page lists where the other product is stronger, where this project differs, and the sources:

- Commercial: [Salesforce](docs/compare/salesforce.md), [HubSpot](docs/compare/hubspot.md),
  [Microsoft Dynamics 365](docs/compare/microsoft-dynamics-365.md), [Zoho CRM](docs/compare/zoho-crm.md),
  [Pipedrive](docs/compare/pipedrive.md)
- Open source: [Twenty](docs/compare/twenty.md), [EspoCRM](docs/compare/espocrm.md),
  [SuiteCRM](docs/compare/suitecrm.md)

## What is different here

- Specification first: [spec](spec/index.md) is the single source of truth for
  both the Rust and Svelte editions.
- Consent-first marketing, explainable rule-based lead scoring, and
  stage-weighted forecasting.
- Contacts are consumed from a separate identity service rather than
  registered here: the CRM holds `person:` and `organization:` references, not
  the records.
- It works with sibling services by reference: won deals open delivery ideas
  in a project portfolio service, and a worker service's hire and leave events
  pause marketing to the organization's own employees.
- Synthetic data only; no real email is sent unless a real mail mode is
  configured.

Corrections and additional comparisons are welcome; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Install and use

## Prerequisites

- Rust 1.100.0 (pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`); the crates declare a minimum of 1.98 (`rust-version`, two releases back)
- PostgreSQL 18 (or `podman compose`)
- Node.js and pnpm, for the front end

## Try it in one command (demo)

From a fresh clone, with no other repository:

```bash
podman compose up --build        # or: docker compose up --build
curl http://localhost:1241/_health/live
```

This starts PostgreSQL, Redis and the API ([compose.yaml](compose.yaml)). **Demo only:** sign-in is off, email is simulated,
and the port is published on this machine's loopback address only. Use synthetic data. The family bridges stay off until you
set their URLs, so nothing here needs the PPM or WPM repositories. For a real deployment, turn authentication on
(see [spec/auth.md](spec/auth.md)) and run with `APP_ENV=production`.

## Rust service

```bash
cd contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust
podman compose -f compose.test.yaml up -d   # test PostgreSQL and Redis
cargo build
cargo test                                   # DB-free unit and request tests
cargo test -- --ignored                      # database-backed tests
```

See the service [README](contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust/README.md)
for the quick start, configuration, and endpoints.

## Sending email

By default the service sends nothing: campaign sends are simulated. To send
real mail, set `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_MODE=smtp` and the `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_*` variables. The
service refuses to start with a bad combination.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_MODE` | `simulated` (default), `smtp`, `brevo`, `mailjet`, `ses`, `azure`, `mailgun` or `sendgrid` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_BREVO_API_KEY` | `brevo` mode: the API key (sent as `api-key`) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAILJET_API_KEY`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAILJET_API_SECRET` | `mailjet` mode: the API key pair (basic auth) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SES_REGION`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | `ses` mode (optional `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SES_SESSION_TOKEN`, and `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SES_CONFIGURATION_SET`, which SES events need). Static keys only; no instance-role lookup |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_AZURE_ENDPOINT`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_AZURE_ACCESS_KEY` | `azure` mode: the Communication Services endpoint and its base64 access key; `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_FROM` must be a verified sender address |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAILGUN_API_KEY`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAILGUN_DOMAIN` | `mailgun` mode (`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAILGUN_API_BASE=https://api.eu.mailgun.net` for the EU region) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAILGUN_SIGNING_KEY` | Mailgun's webhook signing key; Mailgun callbacks are verified with it (not with `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SENDGRID_API_KEY` | `sendgrid` mode |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_API_URL` | Override the vendor endpoint (a test double); `https` in production |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_HOST`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_PORT` | The server; port defaults to 587 (465 with `implicit`) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_TLS` | `starttls` (default), `implicit` or `none` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_USERNAME`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_PASSWORD` | Set together, or neither |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_FROM` | The `From` mailbox, for example `CRM <crm@example.org>` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_BATCH` | Contacts sent per batch (default 200); the job runs batches until done |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_ACCEPT_INVALID_CERTS` | Development only; refused in production |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET` | 32+ characters; signs the unsubscribe link in every message. Required with `smtp` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PUBLIC_URL` | The address recipients reach this service at, for the link (`https` in production). Required with `smtp` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | 32+ characters; enables `POST /webhooks/email` for provider outcomes (delivered, hard or soft bounce, complaint). Requests carry `X-CRM-Timestamp` and `X-CRM-Signature: sha256=` (HMAC-SHA256 of `timestamp.body`); five-minute window |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_ALLOW_PRODUCTION` | Required to use any real mode in production, because the vendor, agreement and legal review is open (CRM-T39) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_DEV_DOMAIN` | Development only: in `stub` upstream mode, mail goes to `<person id>@<domain>` |

With a real sender, `POST /api/campaigns/{pid}/run` checks the campaign and
hands the sending to a background job, answering `202` while it runs (`200`
once complete). In production, `workers.mode` is `BackgroundQueue` (jobs are
kept in PostgreSQL), so run a worker: `cargo run -- start --all`
in development, or a separate `start --worker` process. A campaign whose
remaining sends all fail stops (stays `running`); call `run` again to resume.
Simulated mode, and the test configuration, still finish inside the request.

`POST /api/nurture/advance` mails due nurture steps through the same sender;
each step then needs a `body`.

`brevo` and `mailjet` send through the vendor's HTTP API with `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_FROM`
and the same unsubscribe and webhook settings. Point the vendor's callback at
`POST {CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PUBLIC_URL}/webhooks/email/brevo` (bearer token, or a custom header
`X-CRM-Webhook-Token`) or `/webhooks/email/mailjet` (`https://crm:SECRET@host/…`
basic auth), with `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET` as the secret. For the clouds:
SES publishes events to an SNS topic (add an HTTPS subscription to
`/webhooks/email/ses` with `https://crm:SECRET@host/…`; the service confirms the
subscription itself, for AWS hosts only; SNS message signatures are not
verified); Azure sends delivery reports through Event Grid (a webhook
subscription to `/webhooks/email/azure` with `X-CRM-Webhook-Token` as a
delivery property). Mailgun callbacks go to `/webhooks/email/mailgun` and
SendGrid's Event Webhook to `/webhooks/email/sendgrid` (basic auth in the URL;
SendGrid's ECDSA signature is not verified). Google Cloud has no email-sending
service of its own: use SendGrid or Mailgun, or its SMTP relay with
`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_MODE=smtp` (no outcome callbacks). These adapters follow the vendors'
documentation and have not been run against live accounts.

The CRM holds no email addresses. In `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UPSTREAM_MODE=http` it asks the
person service for an `email` field at send time and stores nothing.

### Local mail server

`scripts/email-dev.sh` runs [Stalwart](https://stalw.art) in Podman and
configures a domain `crm.test` (with a catch-all) and one account:

```bash
scripts/email-dev.sh up      # start and configure (safe to repeat)
scripts/email-dev.sh check   # send a message and read it back
scripts/email-dev.sh live    # run the service's real-SMTP test against it
scripts/email-dev.sh down    # stop; mail is kept
scripts/email-dev.sh reset   # stop and delete all mail
```

To send a campaign through it from the service:

```bash
CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_MODE=smtp CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_HOST=127.0.0.1 CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_PORT=2587 \
CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_USERNAME=crm@crm.test CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_PASSWORD=crm-dev-password \
CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_FROM='CRM <crm@crm.test>' CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_SMTP_ACCEPT_INVALID_CERTS=1 \
CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_MAIL_DEV_DOMAIN=crm.test \
CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UNSUBSCRIBE_SECRET=dev-only-unsubscribe-secret-0123456789 \
CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PUBLIC_URL=http://localhost:1241 cargo run -- start
```

Mail lands in the `crm@crm.test` mailbox; read it over JMAP at
`http://127.0.0.1:8081` (`crm@crm.test` / `crm-dev-password`) or IMAPS on
`2993`. The web admin is the same address (`admin` / `dev-admin-change-me`).
**Development only**: fixed passwords, a self-signed certificate, loopback
ports. Details are in
`contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust/compose.email.yaml`.

## Family bridges

The CRM has four bridges to its sibling services, the project portfolio
service (PPM) and the worker service (WPM), under `/api/bridges`. They are
admin only, except the events route, which is authenticated by its signature:

- a won deal opens a delivery idea in PPM;
- WPM's departments become teams, whose members are `person:` references;
- WPM posts signed hire and leave events that pause and resume a contact's
  marketing;
- the employment check asks WPM which contacts are its workers today.

The outbound bridges are stub-first: nothing leaves the process unless
`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UPSTREAM_MODE=http` is set.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UPSTREAM_MODE` | `http` sends the outbound calls; unset (or anything else) is stub mode |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PPM_SERVICE_URL`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PPM_SERVICE_TOKEN` | PPM's base URL and an optional bearer token |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_URL`, `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_TOKEN` | WPM's base URL and a bearer token. A token is sent only over `https` or to this machine |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_ORGANIZATION_REF` | The `organization:` URN the employment check asks about (CRM-R94). `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_TOKEN` must belong to an HR identity of that organization in WPM. A value that is not an `organization:` URN counts as unset; unset, the check answers `502` in `http` mode |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | 32+ characters; enables `POST /api/bridges/wpm/events` (CRM-R92). Set the same value as WPM's `WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_<NAME>` for the subscription. Requests carry `x-wpm-signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` (HMAC-SHA256 of `t.body`), with a five-minute window. Unset, the route is `404` |

The [family bridges tutorial](docs/tutorial-family-bridges.md) walks through a
signed hire and leave with `openssl` and `curl`, and through the employment
check. None of the bridges has been run against a running WPM or PPM.

## Svelte front end

**Guided tour:** set `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_DEMO_TOUR=on`, start the UI and press **Start the
tour** on `/tour`, or sign in as `example@example.com`. The tour is off when
the setting is absent. No email is sent and no service is needed; every screen shows fictitious data. Each sign-in gets its own copy of the
data, held in memory (at most 200 at a time).

```bash
cd contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

To use a running service instead of the tour, the UI needs the service's
`/api` base in `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_API_URL`. The proxy appends the path after `/api/proxy/`
to this value, and the default, `http://localhost:1241/api`, is a service
started as above, so only the authentication service needs setting:

```bash
AUTH_API_URL=http://localhost:<auth port> pnpm dev
```

A service elsewhere sets the whole base, `/api` included, for example
`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_API_URL=https://crm.example.org/api`; a trailing slash is dropped.

Signing in that way needs the family authentication service at `AUTH_API_URL`
(the UI calls its `/api/auth/magic-link` and `/api/auth/token`). The CRM
service does not provide those routes.

See its [README](contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte/README.md).

## Whole-repo check

```bash
scripts/ci-check.sh <stage>
```

GitHub Actions and Woodpecker run the same stages, so a local pass is the CI pass. The stages:

| Stage | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `fmt`, `clippy` | Rust formatting and lints (warnings are errors), both feature sets |
| `test`, `test-db` | unit tests; the request tests against PostgreSQL |
| `front-end` | `svelte-check`, unit tests with coverage, the build, then `pnpm lint` (Prettier and ESLint) |
| `e2e` | Playwright in a browser, including the guided tour |
| `lint` | spelling (`typos`), GitHub workflow security (`zizmor`) and Markdown (`rumdl`) |
| `mutants` | `cargo mutants` over `src/rules`: it changes each rule a little, and a change no test notices is reported as missed. Slow (hours), so GitHub runs it weekly; run it on one file with `scripts/ci-check.sh mutants --no-config -f src/rules/<file>.rs -- --lib` |
| `api-types` | the UI's generated API types match the service's OpenAPI document |
| `supply-chain` | known vulnerabilities, licences and sources for Rust and the UI, and the SBOMs written to `sbom/` |
| `semver` | the matcher crate's public API against its last published release |
| `scripts` | `shellcheck` on `scripts/*.sh` |
| `coverage` | a Rust line-coverage report from the unit tests (a report, not a gate) |

`typos`, `zizmor` and `rumdl` are installed with `cargo install typos-cli zizmor rumdl`.

This software is not ready for production ([path to production](locales/en-us/path-to-production/index.md)); use synthetic data only.

# Tutorial: run the guided tour

This tutorial starts the user interface on fictional data. It requires no database and no other service.

## Prerequisites

- [Git](https://git-scm.com/)
- Node.js 26
- [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/)

Rust and PostgreSQL are not required for this tutorial.

## Step 1: get the code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/contact-relationship-management/contact-relationship-management.git
cd contact-relationship-management/contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte
```

## Step 2: start the application

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

Open the address that `pnpm dev` prints.

## Step 3: sign in

Sign in as `example@example.com`. This opens the guided tour. Its fictional data is held in the UI server, and no message reaches a real person.

## Step 4: review the tour

The tour page covers six screens.

| Screen | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Contacts | One record for each person, holding a reference and the relationship data |
| Leads | Scores calculated from readable rules |
| Deals | The pipeline by stage |
| Campaigns | Simulated sends and the consent they depend on |
| Tickets | Priorities and service-level deadlines |
| Executive | Summary figures |

## Step 5: change the display settings

The buttons at the top of the page change the language, theme and text size. The interface is available in 21 languages. Arabic displays right to left.

## Next steps

- [Install and use](../INSTALL.md) describes how to start the API, PostgreSQL and Redis with one command.
- [The family bridges](tutorial-family-bridges.md) describes the optional connections to other systems. They are off until configured.
- [Comparisons](../COMPARISONS.md) lists other CRM products.
- [The specification](../spec/index.md) defines the system's behaviour.

This is demonstration software. Use synthetic data only.

# Tutorial: the family bridges

The CRM talks to two sibling services: the project portfolio service (PPM) and the
worker service (WPM). This tutorial sets up the bridges, sends the CRM a signed
hire and leave event the way WPM does, and runs the employment check.

> **Run live against a WPM on 2026-11-01** (a signed hire and leave delivered by
> WPM, then the employment check and the teams import with WPM's sign-in on, and
> a replayed, older, unsigned and unknown event). **Not run against a running
> PPM.** The rest is taken from the
> service's code and request tests (`src/controllers/bridges.rs`,
> `src/rules/wpm_events.rs`, `src/rules/employment_check.rs`, `src/clients.rs`,
> `src/settings.rs`, `tests/requests/wpm_events.rs`,
> `tests/requests/employment_check.rs`). Those tests sign requests with the same
> algorithm WPM uses and answer the employment check from a stand-in WPM. The
> `openssl` signature below was checked against the RFC 4231 test vector the unit
> tests use; the `curl` calls were not run for this tutorial. Use synthetic data
> only.

Paths in this tutorial are relative to
`contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust/`.

## The four bridges

| Route | Direction | What it does | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/bridges/ppm/deals/{pid}` | CRM → PPM | Opens a delivery idea in PPM for a won deal, once per deal | CRM-R72 |
| `POST /api/bridges/wpm/teams-import` | CRM ← WPM | Reads WPM's active workers and sets one CRM team per department; each member is the worker's `person:` reference | CRM-R73 |
| `POST /api/bridges/wpm/events` | WPM → CRM | WPM posts hire and leave events. A hire pauses a contact's marketing; a leave resumes it | CRM-R92, CRM-R93 |
| `POST /api/bridges/wpm/employment-check` | CRM → WPM | Asks WPM which live contacts are its workers today, and marks them as employees | CRM-R94 |

All four are under `/api/bridges`, which is admin only
(`src/auth/policy.rs`, `ADMIN_ONLY_PREFIXES`). The one exception is
`/api/bridges/wpm/events`, which needs no session or bearer token, because the
event's signature authenticates it. The admin rule is enforced only when
`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_REQUIRE_AUTH` is on. It is off by default, so the `curl` calls below need no
token in development.

The three outbound bridges start in **stub mode**. Unless
`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UPSTREAM_MODE=http` is set, nothing leaves the process, and the answer has
`"mode": "stub"` and says what would have been sent. The events route does not
depend on the mode.

A CRM user is a person, named `person:<sign-in subject>` (CRM-D18). Owners,
quota holders and team members all use that form. On input, `worker:<id>` is
still accepted and is stored as `person:<id>`.

## Environment variables

The service reads these settings from the environment once, on first use
(`src/settings.rs`), so restart the service after you change one.

| Variable | Used by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UPSTREAM_MODE` | PPM, teams import, employment check | `http` (any case) sends real requests. Anything else, or unset, means stub mode |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PPM_SERVICE_URL` | PPM bridge | The PPM base URL. The CRM posts `{title, pitch, tags}` to `{url}/api/ideas` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_PPM_SERVICE_TOKEN` | PPM bridge | Optional bearer token, sent only to PPM (CRM-R87, CRM-T153) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_URL` | teams import, employment check | The WPM base URL. The CRM calls `GET {url}/api/workers?status=active&fields=pid,department,person_ref&limit=200&offset=…` (a WPM without `fields`, from before WPM-R216, answers `422` and the import fails) and `POST {url}/api/bridges/overlap` |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_TOKEN` | teams import, employment check | Bearer token, sent only to WPM. The overlap check needs it to belong to an HR identity of the organization below (CRM-D16) |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_ORGANIZATION_REF` | employment check | The `organization:` URN to ask WPM about. A value that is not an `organization:` URN counts as unset |
| `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | events | The shared HMAC secret, at least 32 characters (a shorter value counts as unset). While it is unset, the events route answers `404`. Set the same value as WPM's `WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET_<NAME>` for the subscription |

How the tokens are sent (`src/clients.rs`, `with_credential`):

- A token goes only over `https`, or over `http` to `localhost` or a loopback
  address. For any other `http` address the call fails and nothing is sent.
- The bridge client follows no redirects and gives up after 10 seconds.
- Without a token, the CRM sends no `Authorization` header. That works only
  against a service with authentication off.

## 1. Start the service with a webhook secret

Use the quick start in the [service README](../contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust/README.md)
for the database. Then:

```bash
cd contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust
export CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET='dev-only-wpm-webhook-secret-0123456789'   # 38 characters
cargo run -- start
```

The service listens on `http://localhost:1241` (the default in `src/app.rs`).

## 2. Create a contact for a synthetic person

The events find contacts by `person_ref`, so create a contact with a known
reference and grant marketing consent. The examples use `jq`.

```bash
CRM=http://localhost:1241
PERSON='person:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000101'
ORG='organization:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-0000000000aa'

PID=$(curl -sS -X POST "$CRM/api/contacts" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"person_ref\":\"$PERSON\",\"display_name\":\"Ada Example\"}" | jq -r .pid)

curl -sS -X POST "$CRM/api/contacts/$PID/consent" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"action":"granted","source":"web form"}'
```

## 3. Send a signed hire event

WPM signs each delivery with one header:

```text
x-wpm-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>
```

- The signed message is the timestamp, a `.` and the raw request body, exactly
  the bytes sent. If the body is re-encoded after signing, the signature fails.
- `t` must be within 300 seconds of the CRM's clock, before or after
  (`TOLERANCE_SECS`).
- The `v1` value is lowercase or uppercase hex, compared in constant time. A
  header with `t` or `v1` missing or repeated fails.
- The body may be at most 16 KiB (`MAX_BODY`).
- WPM also sends `x-wpm-event` and `x-wpm-delivery`. The CRM does not read them.

The body is `{id, kind, occurred_at, subject, data}`:

| Member | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | The event id, 1 to 100 characters, the same on every retry. A repeated id changes nothing |
| `kind` | `worker_hired`, `worker_terminated` and `worker_retired` are acted on. `worker_activated` and `leave_approved` are ignored (`not_used`); any other kind is ignored (`unknown_kind`) |
| `occurred_at` | RFC 3339; required for the three kinds acted on. It orders the events (CRM-R93) |
| `subject` | `worker:<pid>`; not read |
| `data` | `person_ref` (a `person:` URN), `organization_ref` (an `organization:` URN) and `effective_on` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). For the two endings WPM also sends `from` and `to`, which the CRM does not read. If `data` is missing (a WPM from before WPM-R207), the event is ignored (`no_data`) |

Sign and send a hire with `openssl` and `curl`:

```bash
SECRET="$CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET"

wpm_send() {   # usage: wpm_send '<json body>'
  local body="$1" t sig
  t=$(date +%s)
  sig=$(printf '%s.%s' "$t" "$body" | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$SECRET" | sed 's/^.*= //')
  curl -sS -X POST "$CRM/api/bridges/wpm/events" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H "x-wpm-signature: t=$t,v1=$sig" \
    --data-binary "$body"
  echo
}

wpm_send "{\"id\":\"evt-0001\",\"kind\":\"worker_hired\",\"occurred_at\":\"2026-10-30T12:00:00Z\",\"subject\":\"worker:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-0000000000f1\",\"data\":{\"person_ref\":\"$PERSON\",\"organization_ref\":\"$ORG\",\"effective_on\":\"2026-11-02\"}}"
```

Use `printf '%s'`, not `echo`, so that no newline is added to the signed text.
Use `--data-binary`, so that `curl` sends the body exactly as signed. The `sed`
removes the `SHA2-256(stdin)=` prefix and its space that OpenSSL prints (checked with OpenSSL 4.1); LibreSSL
prints the bare hex, which the `sed` leaves alone.

The expected answer:

```json
{"result":"paused","reason":null,"contacts":1}
```

The contact is now an employee of the organization:

```bash
curl -sS "$CRM/api/contacts/$PID" | jq .employments
# [{"organization_ref":"organization:3f0c…00aa","since":"2026-11-02"}]
```

While a contact has any employment, segments leave them out, a campaign skips
them ("an employee, by the worker service: marketing paused"), and a nurture step
waits. Their consent does not change. Each change is audited on the contact as
`employment_recorded` or `employment_ended`, with `via: wpm`.

## 4. Send a leave, a repeat and an out-of-order event

```bash
# The leave: a new id, recorded later than the hire.
wpm_send "{\"id\":\"evt-0002\",\"kind\":\"worker_terminated\",\"occurred_at\":\"2026-10-30T13:00:00Z\",\"subject\":\"worker:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-0000000000f1\",\"data\":{\"person_ref\":\"$PERSON\",\"organization_ref\":\"$ORG\",\"effective_on\":\"2026-11-30\",\"from\":\"active\",\"to\":\"terminated\"}}"
# {"result":"resumed","reason":null,"contacts":1}

# The same id again (a WPM retry): nothing changes.
wpm_send "{\"id\":\"evt-0002\",\"kind\":\"worker_terminated\",\"occurred_at\":\"2026-10-30T13:00:00Z\",\"subject\":\"worker:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-0000000000f1\",\"data\":{\"person_ref\":\"$PERSON\",\"organization_ref\":\"$ORG\",\"effective_on\":\"2026-11-30\",\"from\":\"active\",\"to\":\"terminated\"}}"
# {"result":"duplicate","reason":null,"contacts":0}

# A hire recorded before that leave, arriving after it: stale, nothing changes.
wpm_send "{\"id\":\"evt-0003\",\"kind\":\"worker_hired\",\"occurred_at\":\"2026-10-30T12:30:00Z\",\"subject\":\"worker:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-0000000000f1\",\"data\":{\"person_ref\":\"$PERSON\",\"organization_ref\":\"$ORG\",\"effective_on\":\"2026-11-02\"}}"
# {"result":"stale","reason":null,"contacts":0}
```

A leave ends the employment with that organization only. Marketing resumes when
the contact has no employment left, under the consent the contact already had.

Ordering (CRM-R93): the CRM stores the last hire or leave it applied for each
person and organization. Events are compared by `occurred_at`, then by
`effective_on` when two events share the same second. An older event is
`stale`. An event with the same stamp as the last one is applied, so the event
that arrives later wins. The CRM records this order only while the person is a
contact. The retention sweep (`POST /api/retention/sweep`) prunes a stored
leave once it is older than the event retention horizon
(`CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_EVENT_RETENTION_DAYS`, default 30 days, at least 7). An event that arrives
after that is not ordered.

### Answers

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| `404` | `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset or shorter than 32 characters |
| `401` | `x-wpm-signature` is missing, wrong, malformed, or more than 300 seconds old or ahead |
| `400` | The body is not an event (not JSON, no `kind`, or an `id` that is empty or longer than 100 characters) |
| `413` | The body is over 16 KiB |
| `422` | A hire or leave whose `data` is malformed, or whose `occurred_at` is missing or not RFC 3339 |
| `200` | Everything else, with `result`: `paused`, `already_paused`, `resumed`, `not_paused`, `no_contact` (no live contact carries the person), `duplicate`, `stale` or `ignored` (with `reason` `no_data`, `not_used` or `unknown_kind`) |

The CRM answers `200` to events it ignores, so WPM does not retry them.

## 5. The employment check

Events tell the CRM only about hires and leaves that happen after the
subscription. The employment check finds contacts who were already WPM
workers.

In stub mode (the default), it sends nothing and reports what it would ask:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$CRM/api/bridges/wpm/employment-check"
# With only the contact above in the database (asked counts the distinct references):
# {"mode":"stub","organization_ref":null,"asked":1,"batches":1,"workers":0,
#  "recorded":0,"already_paused":0,"left_by_event":0}
```

To ask WPM, restart the service with:

```bash
export CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_UPSTREAM_MODE=http
export CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_URL=https://wpm.example.org          # http is allowed only to this machine
export CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_TOKEN='<token of an HR identity of the organization in WPM>'
export CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_ORGANIZATION_REF='organization:3f0c2b1e-0000-4000-8000-0000000000aa'
```

What the CRM sends (`clients::overlap_check`): `POST
{CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_URL}/api/bridges/overlap` with
`Authorization: Bearer $CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WORKER_SERVICE_TOKEN` and the body

```json
{"organization_ref": "organization:…", "person_refs": ["person:…", "…"]}
```

The body holds each distinct, well-formed `person:` reference of a live contact
once, in sorted order, at most 500 per call. The erasure tombstone and malformed
references are left out, and no name is sent. WPM answers
`{"organization_ref", "results": [{"person_ref", "worker"}]}`.

What happens to the contacts:

- The CRM reads every answer strictly before it writes anything. One failed
  call, a refusal, or a bad answer is `502` and records nothing. A bad answer is
  one for another organization, with no `results`, with a reference that was not
  asked about, or with a reference answered twice. In `http` mode,
  `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_WPM_ORGANIZATION_REF` unset is also `502`.
- For each person WPM says is a worker today, every live contact with that
  reference is marked an employee of the organization from today. This works
  as a hire event does: marketing is paused, consent is unchanged, and the
  change is audited as `employment_recorded` with `via: wpm` and
  `source: employment_check`. The response counts those contacts in `recorded`;
  contacts that were already marked are counted in `already_paused`.
- If the last event applied for that person was a leave, the person is left
  alone and counted in `left_by_event`.
- A "no" changes nothing. The check never ends an employment.
- The check itself is audited once, as `employment_checked` on `bridge`, with
  the counts only and no reference.

The UI has a button for this check on `/quotas`, beside the teams import.

## 6. With authentication on

With `CONTACT_RELATIONSHIP_MANAGEMENT_REQUIRE_AUTH` on, the PPM bridge, the teams import and the employment
check need a bearer token that the ABAC policy allows to perform destructive
actions. Under the built-in policy, that is `access=admin` or a service token.
The events route stays public and is authenticated by its signature alone.

## What is not verified

- Run live against a WPM on 2026-11-01: the events (a hire, a leave, a repeat, an
  older hire, a bad signature, an unknown kind: `paused`, `resumed`, `duplicate`,
  `stale`, `401`, `ignored`), the employment check (3 contacts asked, 2 workers
  recorded, a second run recorded none) and the teams import (one team per
  department), with WPM's sign-in on and an HR token. WPM answers `401` without a
  token and `403` to a token with no HR membership in the organization. Not run
  live: a future `effective_on`, a campaign skipping the contact, and PPM (which
  CRM does not call here). The contracts were first read from the services' source
  (2026-10-28 and 2026-10-30, see the comments in `src/clients.rs`).
- The CRM uses one HR token held by the deployer and one configured
  organization, rather than the caller's own token as WPM-D135 asks (CRM-D16).
  The product owner confirmed this on 2026-10-31 as the accepted design.
- See [spec/integrations.md](../spec/integrations.md#family-bridges) and
  [spec/tasks.md](../spec/tasks.md) (CRM-T139, CRM-T153, CRM-T158 to CRM-T162)
  for the limits recorded with each change.

# Contact Relationship Management — Specification

This directory is the **single source of truth** for the cross-cutting
Contact Relationship Management (CRM) specification, shared by both
editions. Each subproject's own `spec/` adds stack-specific detail and
links back here.

> ⚠️ **Not ready for production.** This project models CRM practice for
> demonstration and integration purposes; it holds no real personal data and
> sends no real email. See the
> [path to production](../locales/en-us/path-to-production/index.md) and
> [regulatory.md](regulatory.md).

## What this project is

A **central hub for managing interactions with customers and
prospects** across the whole relationship lifecycle — first touch to
renewal — organized as four modules:

1. **Sales automation (SFA)** — contact & account management, lead
   capture and scoring, deal pipelines (Kanban), forecasting.
2. **Marketing automation** — email campaigns, segments, lead
   nurturing (drip sequences), campaign tracking & ROI.
3. **Customer service & support** — ticketing, a knowledge base,
   SLA tracking.
4. **Analytics & reporting** — real-time dashboards (win rates,
   pipeline value, customer lifetime value), activity tracking.

It is a **consumer application** (the case-folder / patient-flow /
workforce-planning-management shape): it does not register identities
itself. A contact is a [person-service](../../person/person-service-with-axum/)
record; an account is an
[organization-service](../../organization/organization-service-with-axum/)
record; a sales rep or support agent is a signed-in user, named by
`person:` URN, the sign-in subject (CRM-D18), and the
[worker service](../../worker/worker-service-with-axum/) supplies
departments for teams and hire and leave events (CRM-R73, CRM-R92). CRM
owns only the **relationship and its operational state**: leads,
deals, activities, campaigns, consent, tickets, articles, SLAs —
always referencing identities by `EntityRef` URN, never duplicating
them.

## Two editions

| Subproject                                                                                                         | Role                           | Stack                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| [contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust](../contact-relationship-management-service-with-rust/)         | Back-end JSON API              | Rust, axa (Axum + sqlx), PostgreSQL     |
| [contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte](../contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte/) | Sales / marketing / support UI | SvelteKit 3, Svelte 5 runes, TypeScript |
| [contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-swift](../contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-swift/) | iOS app for reps and agents | Swift 6, SwiftUI, Lily Design System for Swift |
| [contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-kotlin](../contact-relationship-management-mobile-app-with-kotlin/) | Android app for reps and agents | Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Lily Design System for Kotlin |

## Specification (topic files)

| File                                               | Covers                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [purpose.md](purpose.md)                           | Problem statement, goals, the four modules                              |
| [scope.md](scope.md)                               | In/out of scope; the boundary with the identity services                |
| [domain-model.md](domain-model.md)                 | Contact, Account, Lead, Deal, Activity, Campaign, Ticket, SlaPolicy, …  |
| [sales-automation.md](sales-automation.md)         | Module 1: contacts/accounts, lead scoring, pipelines, forecasting       |
| [marketing-automation.md](marketing-automation.md) | Module 2: campaigns, segments, nurture sequences, ROI                   |
| [service-support.md](service-support.md)           | Module 3: tickets, knowledge base, SLA tracking                         |
| [analytics-reporting.md](analytics-reporting.md)   | Module 4: dashboards, KPIs, activity tracking                           |
| [integrations.md](integrations.md)                 | Upstream family services; EntityRef URNs                                |
| [auth.md](auth.md)                                 | SSO, ABAC personas (rep / sales manager / marketing / support), masking |
| [arithmetic/index.md](arithmetic/index.md)         | Math must not panic: `checked_*` and `None`, never a panic or a wrap |
| [audit.md](audit.md)                               | Audit trail, events, consent history                                    |
| [architecture.md](architecture.md)                 | Editions, layering, pure-core rules, persistence                        |
| [testing.md](testing.md)                           | Test strategy per edition                                               |
| [regulatory.md](regulatory.md)                     | Demo status; data-protection and e-privacy (marketing consent) posture  |
| [worldwide.md](worldwide.md)                       | Worldwide equity: CRM-R95 (confirmed), CRM-D19 (confirmed), audit, tasks; CRM-D21 (confirmed, in design.md) |
| [github-pages-site.md](github-pages-site.md)       | The documentation site for GitHub Pages: pages, locales, tests, publish |
| [mobile-apps/index.md](mobile-apps/index.md)       | The iOS and Android apps: screens, rules MOB-1 to MOB-15, Lily, tests  |
| [roadmap.md](roadmap.md)                           | Beyond the v1 queue                                                     |
| [glossary.md](glossary.md)                         | SFA, MQL/SQL, drip, CLV, SLA, …                                         |

## Specification-driven delivery (SDD)

Three lock-step files drive delivery:

- [requirements.md](requirements.md) — numbered requirements (`CRM-R*`)
  with user stories and acceptance criteria.
- [design.md](design.md) — numbered design decisions (`CRM-D*`).
- [tasks.md](tasks.md) — **the live delivery checklist** (`CRM-T*`),
  phased; every task traces to design and requirement ids.

A change starts in `requirements.md`, is shaped in `design.md`, is
queued in `tasks.md`, and only then lands as code in a subproject.
**No code lands without the spec describing it.**

## References

- Sibling consumer apps (the shape this follows):
  [workforce-planning-management](../../workforce-planning-management/spec/index.md),
  [patient-flow](../../patient-flow/spec/index.md),
  [case-folder](../../case-folder/spec/index.md),
  [project-portfolio-management](../../project-portfolio-management/spec/index.md)
- Family contracts:
  [authentication-sessions](../../agents/share/authentication-sessions.md),
  [authorization-attributes](../../agents/share/authorization-attributes.md),
  [security](../../agents/share/security.md),
  [privacy](../../agents/share/privacy.md) (the person-service consent
  model CRM's marketing consent mirrors)

  The `agents/share/` documents (here and in code comments as
  `agents/share/*.md`) belong to the product family's shared repository,
  `main-x-service`, not to this one. These links resolve only in a checkout
  where this repository sits beside that one's `agents/` directory; elsewhere
  they are dangling, and the comments name the contract that the code follows.
- **Local-first CI/CD (proposed):** [local-ci-cd.md](local-ci-cd.md).

## Two locale sets (CRM-T89)

The repository has two sets of locales, for two different things, and they are not meant to be equal.

| Set | What it translates | Locales |
|---|---|---|
| `locales/` (this page) | The 11 role briefs | 11 directories: `ar-001`, `cy-001`, `cy-gb`, `en-001`, `en-gb`, `en-gb-oxendict`, `en-us`, `hi-001`, `hi-in`, `zh-001`, `zh-cn` |
| The UI (`src/lib/locales/*.ts`) | The interface strings (counted in the [translation-review register](../../contact-relationship-management-ui-with-svelte/spec/translation-register.md)) | 8: `ar-001`, `cy-001`, `de-de`, `en-001`, `es-001`, `fr-001`, `hi-001`, `zh-cn` |

- The briefs have regional variants the UI does not (`cy-gb`, `en-gb`, `en-us`, `en-gb-oxendict`, `hi-in`,
  `zh-001`). The UI picks a locale by language, so each of them resolves to a UI locale (`en-gb` to `en-001`,
  `hi-in` to `hi-001`, `zh-001` to `zh-cn`). A UI test reads this directory and fails if a brief locale would
  fall back to English.
- The UI has three languages the briefs do not (`de-de`, `es-001`, `fr-001`). A reader who chooses one of them
  gets the UI in their language and the briefs in English until a brief is translated.
- Each UI locale is one module loaded on demand; `scripts/identical-to-english.mjs` lists the values that match
  English, for native reviewers (`spec/locale-review.md` in the UI folder).

## Rules applied

- Each topic directory has `index.md`, a `README.md` symlink to it, and a
  `.locale-peer-id`. The id is the same 32-character hexadecimal value in every
  locale for the same topic, regardless of slug.
- English locales keep English slugs; the Chinese, Hindi and Welsh locales use
  native-language slugs, and the links between role briefs point at them.
- Kept untranslated on purpose: code, commands, identifiers, file names, task
  numbers (T39 and so on), product and standard names (PostgreSQL, Redis, HIPAA,
  GDPR, NHS DTAC, WCAG), and proper nouns.

# Privacy notice: what is kept in your browser

This notice covers two things: this website (`contact-relationship-management.github.io`), and the Contact
Relationship Management user interface as this repository ships it. It lists everything either one stores in your
browser, and why.

An organization that runs the CRM processes personal data about its contacts. That processing is covered by that
organization's own privacy notice, not this one ([spec/regulatory.md](../spec/regulatory.md)).

## What is stored, and why

Each item holds a choice that you made: a theme, a language and locale, a text size, a time zone, or the layout of
a table. None of them holds your name, email address, IP address or any identifier, and none of them is used to
track you, measure you or show you advertising. Each one exists so that the next page you open uses the same
choice, and you do not have to make it again.

Nothing is stored until you make a choice. A visitor who changes nothing has nothing stored.

### On this website

| Name | Kind | What it holds | Kept for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lily-theme` | Cookie and `localStorage` | `system` ("Follow this device") or the name of a theme, such as `dark` | Cookie: 400 days. `localStorage`: until you clear it |
| `lily-text-size` | `localStorage` | The text size you picked | Until you clear it |
| `lily-time-zone` | `localStorage` | The time zone you picked | Until you clear it |

The theme is kept in a cookie and in `localStorage`, so that it is still there if your browser clears one of them.
The site's pages are static files, and no program on the site reads the cookie. Because it is a cookie, your browser
sends it to GitHub Pages, which hosts the site, with each request to the site.

The site's language and locale are part of the page address, such as `/de-de/`, so nothing is stored for them.

### In the CRM user interface

| Name | Kind | What it holds | Kept for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `crm-theme` | Cookie | `system` ("Follow this device") or the name of a theme | 400 days |
| `mxi.crm.locale` | `localStorage` | The language and locale you picked, such as `de-de` | Until you clear it |
| `lily-text-size` | `localStorage` | The text size you picked | Until you clear it |
| `crm-grid-<table>` | `localStorage` | One table's column widths, hidden columns and sort order | Until you clear it |
| `crm-grid-order-<table>` | `localStorage` | One table's column order | Until you clear it |
| `__Host-mxi_session` | Cookie | A random identifier for your signed-in session | Until you sign out or the session ends |

The CRM's server reads the `crm-theme` cookie, so that it can send each page in your theme and the page does not
first appear in another one. The CRM never reads it for any other purpose.

The session cookie is not a choice. It is set when you sign in, the browser's scripts cannot read it (`HttpOnly`),
and without it you cannot stay signed in.

## Who receives it

These items stay in your browser. Nothing in them is sent to a third party, apart from the site's theme cookie,
which your browser sends to the site's host as described above. Cookies are first party (`SameSite=Lax`), and
`Secure` on an `https` page.

## How to remove it

To change a choice, make it again. To remove everything, clear this site's data in your browser's settings: the
next page then uses the defaults again, which means following your device's light or dark setting, the standard
text size and the page's default language.

# Contact Relationship Management and EspoCRM

EspoCRM is a free, open-source CRM written in PHP. Contact Relationship Management is open-source software that is not ready for production ([path to production](../../locales/en-us/path-to-production/index.md)). The two are not direct alternatives.

## Summary

| | EspoCRM | Contact Relationship Management |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category | Free, open-source CRM platform | Open-source demonstration software, driven by its specification |
| Licence | GNU AGPLv3 | MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, GPL-2.0-only, GPL-3.0-only, OGL-UK-3.0 or CC-BY-SA-4.0, at the user's option |
| Hosting | Self-hosted by script, by hand or with Docker | Self-hosted: a Rust service, a Svelte interface and PostgreSQL |
| Focus | Leads, contacts, sales, marketing and support cases | Sales, marketing, support and analytics, with recorded consent |

## Where EspoCRM is stronger

- Broader features. This project is a demonstration.
- Working product with an online demo that requires no installation.
- Supports MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL.

## Where this project differs

- Emphasizes explainable rules for scoring and forecasting.
- Built in Rust and Svelte, with the specification as the source of truth.
- Stores a reference to a person, not a copy of their details.

## Suitability

- EspoCRM suits organizations that need a broad open-source CRM on a PHP stack.
- This project suits a small reference with explainable rules.

See the [tutorial](../tutorial-first-tour.md) and [all comparisons](../../COMPARISONS.md).

## Sources

# Contact Relationship Management and Zoho CRM

Zoho CRM is a commercial CRM with a free edition. Contact Relationship Management is open-source software that is not ready for production ([path to production](../../locales/en-us/path-to-production/index.md)). The two are not direct alternatives.

## Summary

| | Zoho CRM | Contact Relationship Management |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Category | CRM combining automation with an accessible interface | Open-source demonstration software, driven by its specification |
| Licence | Commercial, with a free edition for a small number of users | MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, GPL-2.0-only, GPL-3.0-only, OGL-UK-3.0 or CC-BY-SA-4.0, at the user's option |
| Hosting | Hosted by Zoho | Self-hosted: a Rust service, a Svelte interface and PostgreSQL |
| Focus | Sales automation, CPQ, forecasting and multichannel engagement | Sales, marketing, support and analytics, with recorded consent |

## Where Zoho CRM is stronger

- Supported commercial product with a free edition. This project is demonstration software.
- Includes CPQ, sales force automation and real-time multichannel engagement.
- A separate product, Bigin, is aimed at small businesses.

## Where this project differs

- The whole system can be self-hosted and inspected.
- Sending without recorded consent is prevented by design.
- Stores a reference to a person, not a copy of their details.

## Suitability

- Zoho CRM suits small businesses that need a hosted CRM.
- This project suits inspecting or adapting the software.

See the [tutorial](../tutorial-first-tour.md) and [all comparisons](../../COMPARISONS.md).

## Sources

Statements about Zoho CRM are based on the public pages below, checked on 2026-11-04. Product details change. Corrections are welcome; see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../CONTRIBUTING.md).

- [Zoho CRM](https://www.zoho.com/crm/)

Zoho CRM is a trademark of its owner. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by it.

# إدارة علاقات جهات الاتصال

برنامج مفتوح المصدر لإدارة العلاقات في المبيعات والتسويق ودعم العملاء.

تتتبّع إدارة علاقات جهات الاتصال العلاقات مع العملاء والعملاء المحتملين في المبيعات والتسويق والدعم. وتحتفظ بسجل واحد لكل جهة اتصال، وتشترط تسجيل الموافقة قبل إرسال أي رسالة. هذا البرنامج ليس جاهزًا لبيئة الإنتاج، ويعمل ببيانات اصطناعية.

## الفوائد

- **سجل واحد لجهة الاتصال.** تستخدم المبيعات والتسويق والدعم والتحليلات السجل نفسه.
- **موافقة مسجّلة.** لا يُرسَل أي شيء إلى جهة اتصال دون موافقة مسجّلة. ويتضمن كل بريد إلكتروني رابط إلغاء اشتراك موقّعًا.
- **بيانات شخصية أقل.** يخزّن نظام CRM مرجعًا إلى الشخص في خدمة الهوية، لا نسخة من الاسم أو العنوان.
- **نتائج قابلة للتفسير.** تُحسب درجات العملاء المحتملين من قواعد مقروءة، وتُحسب التوقعات من مراحل مرجّحة في مسار المبيعات.
- **تصميم دولي.** لا ترتبط الأسماء والعناوين والتقاويم واتجاهات الكتابة بتنسيق بلد واحد. وتتوفر الواجهة بثماني لغات.
- **مواصفات عامة.** المواصفات والشيفرة والاختبارات متاحة للعموم. وتوضّح الوثائق ما بُني وما لم يُبنَ.

## الميزات

- **المبيعات.** تقييم العملاء المحتملين بالقواعد، ومسارات صفقات على لوحة، وتوقعات مرجّحة بالمراحل.
- **التسويق.** حملات مجزّأة وتسلسلات رعاية. ويكون الإرسال محاكاةً ما لم يُضبط وضع للبريد.
- **الدعم.** تذاكر ذات أولويات ومواعيد نهائية لمستوى الخدمة، ومقالات قاعدة المعرفة.
- **التحليلات.** لوحات معلومات لمعدل الفوز، والمسار بحسب المرحلة، وعائد الحملات، وسلامة مستوى الخدمة، والقيمة الدائمة للعميل.
- **جودة البيانات.** كشف السجلات المكررة بالاحتمال، مع الدمج والتراجع.
- **الحوكمة.** سجل تدقيق، ووصول قائم على الأدوار، ودعم طلبات وصول صاحب البيانات وطلبات المحو.

## البدء

1. **احصل على الشيفرة.** استنسخ المستودع. يلزم Node.js و pnpm.
2. **شغّل التطبيق.** في دليل Svelte، نفّذ `pnpm install` ثم `pnpm dev`.
3. **سجّل الدخول.** استخدم `example@example.com`. لا تلزم أي خدمة أخرى.
4. **راجع الجولة.** تغطي الجولة جهات الاتصال والعملاء المحتملين والصفقات والحملات والتذاكر والعرض التنفيذي، باستخدام بيانات خيالية.

يصف [الدرس التعليمي](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) (بالإنجليزية) كل خطوة. ويغطي [التثبيت والاستخدام](../../INSTALL.md) (بالإنجليزية) الخدمة الكاملة.

## المقارنة

| المشروع | الفئة | الفرق |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Twenty](../../docs/compare/twenty.md) | CRM مفتوح المصدر | منتج كامل. هذا المشروع عرض توضيحي أصغر قائم على المواصفات. |
| [EspoCRM](../../docs/compare/espocrm.md) | CRM مفتوح المصدر | ميزات أوسع. يركّز هذا المشروع على القواعد القابلة للتفسير. |
| [SuiteCRM](../../docs/compare/suitecrm.md) | CRM مفتوح المصدر | ناضج وكبير. هذا المشروع مرجع مدمج. |
| [Salesforce](../../docs/compare/salesforce.md)، [HubSpot](../../docs/compare/hubspot.md) | CRM تجاري بنموذج SaaS | يحاكي هذا المشروع الممارسة نفسها. ولا تُشارَك أي شيفرة أو بيانات. |

هذا المشروع عرض توضيحي ولا ينافس هذه المنتجات. راجع [جميع المقارنات](../../COMPARISONS.md) (بالإنجليزية).

## إحاطات الأدوار

توفّر [إحاطات الأدوار](for/) صفحة واحدة لكل دور قيادي: ما يفعله البرنامج، وما لا يفعله، والقرارات التي تعود إلى ذلك الدور.

## الحالة

هذا البرنامج ليس جاهزًا لبيئة الإنتاج ([الطريق إلى بيئة الإنتاج](path-to-production/index.md)). استخدم بيانات اصطناعية فقط. لا يُرسَل بريد حقيقي ما لم يُضبط وضع بريد حقيقي. لا شيء في هذا الموقع يُعدّ مشورة قانونية.

# কন্টাক্ট রিলেশনশিপ ম্যানেজমেন্ট

বিক্রয়, বিপণন ও গ্রাহক সহায়তার জন্য ওপেন-সোর্স সিআরএম সফটওয়্যার।

কন্টাক্ট রিলেশনশিপ ম্যানেজমেন্ট বিক্রয়, বিপণন ও সহায়তা জুড়ে গ্রাহক ও সম্ভাব্য গ্রাহকের সম্পর্ক নথিভুক্ত রাখে। প্রতিটি যোগাযোগের জন্য এটি একটিমাত্র রেকর্ড রাখে এবং বার্তা পাঠানোর আগে লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি আবশ্যক করে। সফটওয়্যারটি উৎপাদনের জন্য প্রস্তুত নয়: এটি কৃত্রিম ডেটার উপর চলে।

## সুবিধা

- **একক যোগাযোগ রেকর্ড।** বিক্রয়, বিপণন, সহায়তা ও বিশ্লেষণ একই রেকর্ড ব্যবহার করে।
- **লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি।** লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি ছাড়া কোনো যোগাযোগকারীকে কিছু পাঠানো হয় না। প্রতিটি ই-মেইলে স্বাক্ষরিত আনসাবস্ক্রাইব লিংক থাকে।
- **কম ব্যক্তিগত ডেটা।** সিআরএম নাম বা ঠিকানার অনুলিপি রাখে না; এটি পরিচয় পরিষেবায় থাকা ব্যক্তির একটি রেফারেন্স রাখে।
- **ব্যাখ্যাযোগ্য ফলাফল।** লিড স্কোর পড়ার যোগ্য নিয়ম থেকে গণনা করা হয়। পূর্বাভাস ভারযুক্ত পাইপলাইন ধাপ থেকে গণনা করা হয়।
- **আন্তর্জাতিক নকশা।** নাম, ঠিকানা, ক্যালেন্ডার ও লেখার দিক কোনো একটি দেশের বিন্যাসের সঙ্গে বাঁধা নয়। ইন্টারফেস আটটি ভাষায় পাওয়া যায়।
- **প্রকাশ্য স্পেসিফিকেশন।** স্পেসিফিকেশন, কোড ও পরীক্ষা সবই প্রকাশ্য। ডকুমেন্টেশনে বলা আছে কী তৈরি হয়েছে এবং কী হয়নি।

## বৈশিষ্ট্য

- **বিক্রয়।** নিয়মভিত্তিক লিড স্কোরিং, বোর্ডে ডিল পাইপলাইন এবং ধাপ-ভারযুক্ত পূর্বাভাস।
- **বিপণন।** বিভাজিত প্রচারণা ও লালন-ক্রম। মেইল মোড কনফিগার না করলে পাঠানো অনুকরণ করা হয়।
- **সহায়তা।** অগ্রাধিকার ও সেবা-স্তরের সময়সীমাসহ টিকিট এবং জ্ঞানভান্ডারের নিবন্ধ।
- **বিশ্লেষণ।** জয়ের হার, ধাপ অনুযায়ী পাইপলাইন, প্রচারণার প্রতিদান, সেবা-স্তরের স্বাস্থ্য ও গ্রাহকের আজীবন মূল্যের ড্যাশবোর্ড।
- **ডেটার মান।** সম্ভাবনা অনুযায়ী ডুপ্লিকেট শনাক্তকরণ, একীকরণ ও পূর্বাবস্থায় ফেরানোসহ।
- **শাসন।** অডিট লগ, ভূমিকাভিত্তিক প্রবেশাধিকার এবং বিষয়-প্রবেশাধিকার ও মুছে ফেলার অনুরোধে সহায়তা।

## শুরু করা

1. **কোড নিন।** রিপোজিটরি ক্লোন করুন। Node.js ও pnpm প্রয়োজন।
2. **অ্যাপ্লিকেশন চালু করুন।** Svelte ডিরেক্টরিতে `pnpm install` চালান, তারপর `pnpm dev`।
3. **সাইন ইন করুন।** `example@example.com` ব্যবহার করুন। অন্য কোনো পরিষেবা লাগে না।
4. **ভ্রমণ দেখুন।** ভ্রমণে কাল্পনিক ডেটা দিয়ে যোগাযোগ, লিড, ডিল, প্রচারণা, টিকিট ও নির্বাহী দৃশ্য দেখানো হয়।

[টিউটোরিয়াল](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) প্রতিটি ধাপ বর্ণনা করে। [ইনস্টল ও ব্যবহার](../../INSTALL.md) সম্পূর্ণ পরিষেবা নিয়ে।

# কন্টাক্ট রিলেশনশিপ ম্যানেজমেন্ট

বিক্রয়, বিপণন ও গ্রাহক সহায়তার জন্য ওপেন-সোর্স সিআরএম সফটওয়্যার।

কন্টাক্ট রিলেশনশিপ ম্যানেজমেন্ট বিক্রয়, বিপণন ও সহায়তা জুড়ে গ্রাহক ও সম্ভাব্য গ্রাহকের সম্পর্ক নথিভুক্ত রাখে। প্রতিটি যোগাযোগের জন্য এটি একটিমাত্র রেকর্ড রাখে এবং বার্তা পাঠানোর আগে লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি আবশ্যক করে। সফটওয়্যারটি উৎপাদনের জন্য প্রস্তুত নয়: এটি কৃত্রিম ডেটার উপর চলে।

- **আন্তর্জাতিক নকশা।** নাম, ঠিকানা, ক্যালেন্ডার ও লেখার দিক কোনো একটি দেশের বিন্যাসের সঙ্গে বাঁধা নয়। ইন্টারফেস আটটি ভাষায় পাওয়া যায়।

# কন্টাক্ট রিলেশনশিপ ম্যানেজমেন্ট

বিক্রয়, বিপণন ও গ্রাহক সহায়তার জন্য ওপেন-সোর্স সিআরএম সফ্টওয়্যার।

কন্টাক্ট রিলেশনশিপ ম্যানেজমেন্ট বিক্রয়, বিপণন ও সহায়তা জুড়ে গ্রাহক ও সম্ভাব্য গ্রাহকের সম্পর্ক নথিভুক্ত রাখে। প্রতিটি যোগাযোগের জন্য এটি একটিমাত্র রেকর্ড রাখে এবং বার্তা পাঠানোর আগে লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি আবশ্যক করে। সফ্টওয়্যারটি উৎপাদনের জন্য প্রস্তুত নয়: এটি কৃত্রিম ডেটার উপর চলে।

## সুবিধা

- **একক যোগাযোগ রেকর্ড।** বিক্রয়, বিপণন, সহায়তা ও বিশ্লেষণ একই রেকর্ড ব্যবহার করে।
- **লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি।** লিপিবদ্ধ সম্মতি ছাড়া কোনো যোগাযোগকারীকে কিছু পাঠানো হয় না। প্রতিটি ইমেলে স্বাক্ষরিত আনসাবস্ক্রাইব লিংক থাকে।
- **কম ব্যক্তিগত ডেটা।** সিআরএম নাম বা ঠিকানার অনুলিপি রাখে না; এটি পরিচয় পরিষেবায় থাকা ব্যক্তির একটি রেফারেন্স রাখে।
- **ব্যাখ্যাযোগ্য ফলাফল।** লিড স্কোর পড়ার যোগ্য নিয়ম থেকে গণনা করা হয়। পূর্বাভাস ভারযুক্ত পাইপলাইন ধাপ থেকে গণনা করা হয়।
- **আন্তর্জাতিক নকশা।** নাম, ঠিকানা, ক্যালেন্ডার ও লেখার দিক কোনো একটি দেশের বিন্যাসের সঙ্গে বাঁধা নয়। ইন্টারফেস আটটি ভাষায় পাওয়া যায়।
- **প্রকাশ্য স্পেসিফিকেশন।** স্পেসিফিকেশন, কোড ও পরীক্ষা সবই প্রকাশ্য। ডকুমেন্টেশনে বলা আছে কী তৈরি হয়েছে এবং কী হয়নি।

## বৈশিষ্ট্য

- **বিক্রয়।** নিয়মভিত্তিক লিড স্কোরিং, বোর্ডে ডিল পাইপলাইন এবং ধাপ-ভারযুক্ত পূর্বাভাস।
- **বিপণন।** বিভাজিত প্রচারণা ও লালন-ক্রম। মেইল মোড কনফিগার না করলে পাঠানো অনুকরণ করা হয়।
- **সহায়তা।** অগ্রাধিকার ও সেবা-স্তরের সময়সীমাসহ টিকিট এবং জ্ঞানভান্ডারের নিবন্ধ।
- **বিশ্লেষণ।** জয়ের হার, ধাপ অনুযায়ী পাইপলাইন, প্রচারণার প্রতিদান, সেবা-স্তরের স্বাস্থ্য ও গ্রাহকের আজীবন মূল্যের ড্যাশবোর্ড।
- **ডেটার মান।** সম্ভাবনা অনুযায়ী ডুপ্লিকেট শনাক্তকরণ, একীকরণ ও পূর্বাবস্থায় ফেরানোসহ।
- **শাসন।** অডিট লগ, ভূমিকাভিত্তিক প্রবেশাধিকার এবং বিষয়-প্রবেশাধিকার ও মুছে ফেলার অনুরোধে সহায়তা।

## শুরু করা

1. **কোড নিন।** রিপোজিটরি ক্লোন করুন। Node.js ও pnpm প্রয়োজন।
2. **অ্যাপ্লিকেশন চালু করুন।** Svelte ডিরেক্টরিতে `pnpm install` চালান, তারপর `pnpm dev`।
3. **সাইন ইন করুন।** `example@example.com` ব্যবহার করুন। অন্য কোনো পরিষেবা লাগে না।
4. **ভ্রমণ দেখুন।** ভ্রমণে কাল্পনিক ডেটা দিয়ে যোগাযোগ, লিড, ডিল, প্রচারণা, টিকিট ও নির্বাহী দৃশ্য দেখানো হয়।

[টিউটোরিয়াল](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) প্রতিটি ধাপ বর্ণনা করে। [ইনস্টল ও ব্যবহার](../../INSTALL.md) সম্পূর্ণ পরিষেবা নিয়ে।

## তুলনা

| প্রকল্প | শ্রেণি | পার্থক্য |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Twenty](../../docs/compare/twenty.md) | ওপেন-সোর্স সিআরএম | পূর্ণাঙ্গ পণ্য। এই প্রকল্প একটি ছোট, স্পেসিফিকেশন-চালিত প্রদর্শনী। |
| [EspoCRM](../../docs/compare/espocrm.md) | ওপেন-সোর্স সিআরএম | বিস্তৃততর বৈশিষ্ট্য। এই প্রকল্প ব্যাখ্যাযোগ্য নিয়মে জোর দেয়। |
| [SuiteCRM](../../docs/compare/suitecrm.md) | ওপেন-সোর্স সিআরএম | পরিণত ও বড়। এই প্রকল্প একটি সংক্ষিপ্ত রেফারেন্স। |
| [Salesforce](../../docs/compare/salesforce.md), [HubSpot](../../docs/compare/hubspot.md) | বাণিজ্যিক SaaS সিআরএম | এই প্রকল্প একই চর্চার মডেল তৈরি করে। কোনো কোড বা ডেটা ভাগ করা হয় না। |

এই প্রকল্প একটি প্রদর্শনী এবং এসব পণ্যের সঙ্গে প্রতিযোগিতা করে না। [সব তুলনা](../../COMPARISONS.md) দেখুন।

## ভূমিকা-সংক্ষেপ

[ভূমিকা-সংক্ষেপ](জন্য/) প্রতিটি জ্যেষ্ঠ ভূমিকার জন্য একটি করে পৃষ্ঠা দেয়: সফ্টওয়্যার কী করে, কী করে না, এবং কোন সিদ্ধান্তগুলো সেই ভূমিকার।

## অবস্থা

এই সফ্টওয়্যার উৎপাদনের জন্য প্রস্তুত নয় ([উৎপাদনের পথ](উৎপাদনের-পথ/index.md))। শুধু কৃত্রিম ডেটা ব্যবহার করুন। প্রকৃত মেইল মোড কনফিগার না করলে কোনো প্রকৃত ইমেল পাঠানো হয় না। এই সাইটের কিছুই আইনি পরামর্শ নয়।

# Rheoli Perthnasoedd Cyswllt

Meddalwedd CRM ffynhonnell agored ar gyfer gwerthu, marchnata a chymorth i gwsmeriaid.

Mae Rheoli Perthnasoedd Cyswllt yn olrhain perthnasoedd â chwsmeriaid a darpar gwsmeriaid ar draws gwerthu, marchnata a chymorth. Mae'n cadw un cofnod ar gyfer pob cyswllt ac mae angen caniatâd wedi'i gofnodi cyn anfon neges. Nid yw'r feddalwedd yn barod ar gyfer cynhyrchu: mae'n rhedeg ar ddata synthetig.

## Manteision

- **Un cofnod cyswllt.** Mae gwerthu, marchnata, cymorth a dadansoddeg yn defnyddio'r un cofnod.
- **Caniatâd wedi'i gofnodi.** Nid anfonir dim at gyswllt heb ganiatâd wedi'i gofnodi. Mae pob e-bost yn cynnwys dolen dad-danysgrifio wedi'i llofnodi.
- **Llai o ddata personol.** Mae'r CRM yn storio cyfeiriad at berson mewn gwasanaeth hunaniaeth, nid copi o'r enw na'r cyfeiriad post.
- **Canlyniadau esboniadwy.** Cyfrifir sgoriau arweinwyr o reolau darllenadwy. Cyfrifir rhagolygon o gamau piblinell wedi'u pwysoli.
- **Dylunio rhyngwladol.** Nid yw enwau, cyfeiriadau, calendrau a chyfeiriadau ysgrifennu ynghlwm wrth fformat un wlad. Mae'r rhyngwyneb ar gael mewn wyth iaith.
- **Manyleb gyhoeddus.** Mae'r fanyleb, y cod a'r profion yn gyhoeddus. Mae'r ddogfennaeth yn nodi beth sydd wedi'i adeiladu a beth sydd heb ei adeiladu.

## Nodweddion

- **Gwerthu.** Sgorio arweinwyr yn ôl rheolau, piblinellau bargeinion ar fwrdd, a rhagolygon wedi'u pwysoli fesul cam.
- **Marchnata.** Ymgyrchoedd wedi'u segmentu a dilyniannau meithrin. Mae anfon wedi'i efelychu oni bai bod modd post wedi'i ffurfweddu.
- **Cymorth.** Tocynnau gyda blaenoriaethau a therfynau amser lefel gwasanaeth, ac erthyglau sylfaen wybodaeth.
- **Dadansoddeg.** Dangosfyrddau ar gyfer cyfradd ennill, piblinell fesul cam, enillion ymgyrch, iechyd lefel gwasanaeth a gwerth oes cwsmer.
- **Ansawdd data.** Canfod dyblygiadau yn ôl tebygolrwydd, gyda chyfuno a dadwneud.
- **Llywodraethu.** Log archwilio, mynediad yn ôl rôl, a chymorth ar gyfer ceisiadau mynediad gwrthrych a dileu.

## Dechrau arni

1. **Cael y cod.** Clonio'r ystorfa. Mae angen Node.js a pnpm.
2. **Dechrau'r rhaglen.** Yn y cyfeiriadur Svelte, rhedwch `pnpm install`, yna `pnpm dev`.
3. **Mewngofnodi.** Defnyddiwch `example@example.com`. Nid oes angen unrhyw wasanaeth arall.
4. **Adolygu'r daith.** Mae'r daith yn ymdrin â chysylltiadau, arweinwyr, bargeinion, ymgyrchoedd, tocynnau a'r olwg weithredol, gan ddefnyddio data ffuglennol.

Mae'r [tiwtorial](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) (Saesneg) yn disgrifio pob cam. Mae [gosod a defnyddio](../../INSTALL.md) (Saesneg) yn ymdrin â'r gwasanaeth llawn.

## Cymhariaeth

| Prosiect | Categori | Gwahaniaeth |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Twenty](../../docs/compare/twenty.md) | CRM ffynhonnell agored | Cynnyrch llawn. Arddangosiad llai wedi'i yrru gan fanyleb yw'r prosiect hwn. |
| [EspoCRM](../../docs/compare/espocrm.md) | CRM ffynhonnell agored | Nodweddion ehangach. Mae'r prosiect hwn yn pwysleisio rheolau esboniadwy. |
| [SuiteCRM](../../docs/compare/suitecrm.md) | CRM ffynhonnell agored | Aeddfed a mawr. Cyfeirnod cryno yw'r prosiect hwn. |
| [Salesforce](../../docs/compare/salesforce.md), [HubSpot](../../docs/compare/hubspot.md) | CRM SaaS masnachol | Mae'r prosiect hwn yn modelu'r un arfer. Ni rennir cod na data. |

Arddangosiad yw'r prosiect hwn ac nid yw'n cystadlu â'r cynhyrchion hyn. Gweler [pob cymhariaeth](../../COMPARISONS.md) (Saesneg).

## Briffiau rôl

Mae'r [briffiau rôl](for/) yn darparu un dudalen ar gyfer pob uwch rôl: beth mae'r feddalwedd yn ei wneud, beth nad yw'n ei wneud, a pha benderfyniadau sy'n perthyn i'r rôl honno.

## Statws

Nid yw'r feddalwedd hon yn barod ar gyfer cynhyrchu ([y llwybr i gynhyrchu](path-to-production/index.md)). Defnyddiwch ddata synthetig yn unig. Nid anfonir e-bost go iawn oni bai bod modd post go iawn wedi'i ffurfweddu. Nid oes dim ar y wefan hon yn gyngor cyfreithiol.

# Contact Relationship Management

CRM-software med åben kildekode til salg, marketing og kundesupport.

Contact Relationship Management følger kunde- og emnerelationer på tværs af salg, marketing og support. Systemet har én post for hver kontakt og kræver registreret samtykke, før en besked sendes. Softwaren er ikke klar til produktion: den kører på syntetiske data.

## Fordele

- **Én kontaktpost.** Salg, marketing, support og analyse bruger den samme post.
- **Registreret samtykke.** Intet sendes til en kontakt uden registreret samtykke. Hver e-mail indeholder et signeret afmeldingslink.
- **Færre personoplysninger.** CRM-systemet gemmer en henvisning til en person i en identitetstjeneste, ikke en kopi af navn eller adresse.
- **Forklarlige resultater.** Lead-scores beregnes ud fra læsbare regler. Prognoser beregnes ud fra vægtede faser i pipelinen.
- **International opbygning.** Navne, adresser, kalendere og skriveretninger er ikke bundet til ét lands format. Brugerfladen findes på otte sprog.
- **Offentlig specifikation.** Specifikationen, koden og testene er offentlige. Dokumentationen angiver, hvad der er bygget, og hvad der ikke er.

## Funktioner

- **Salg.** Regelbaseret lead-scoring, deal-pipelines på en tavle og prognoser vægtet efter fase.
- **Marketing.** Segmenterede kampagner og nurture-forløb. Udsendelsen er simuleret, medmindre en mailtilstand er konfigureret.
- **Support.** Sager med prioriteter og frister for serviceniveau samt artikler i vidensbasen.
- **Analyse.** Dashboards for vinderrate, pipeline pr. fase, afkast af kampagner, status for serviceniveau og kundens livstidsværdi.
- **Datakvalitet.** Registrering af dubletter efter sandsynlighed, med sammenlægning og fortryd.
- **Styring.** Revisionslog, rollebaseret adgang og understøttelse af anmodninger om indsigt og sletning.

## Kom i gang

1. **Hent koden.** Klon repositoriet. Node.js og pnpm er påkrævet.
2. **Start programmet.** Kør `pnpm install` og derefter `pnpm dev` i Svelte-mappen.
3. **Log ind.** Brug `example@example.com`. Ingen anden tjeneste er nødvendig.
4. **Gennemgå rundvisningen.** Rundvisningen dækker kontakter, leads, deals, kampagner, sager og ledelsesoversigten med fiktive data.

[Vejledningen](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) beskriver hvert trin. [Installation og brug](../../INSTALL.md) dækker hele tjenesten.

Denne software er ikke klar til produktion ([vej til produktion](vej-til-produktion/index.md)). Brug kun syntetiske data. Der sendes ingen rigtig e-mail, medmindre en rigtig mailtilstand er konfigureret. Intet på dette websted er juridisk rådgivning.

# Contact Relationship Management

Open-Source-CRM-Software für Vertrieb, Marketing und Kundenservice.

Contact Relationship Management verwaltet Beziehungen zu Kunden und Interessenten in Vertrieb, Marketing und Service. Die Software führt für jeden Kontakt genau einen Datensatz und verlangt eine dokumentierte Einwilligung, bevor eine Nachricht versendet wird. Sie ist nicht produktionsreif: Sie arbeitet mit synthetischen Daten.

## Vorteile

- **Ein Kontaktdatensatz.** Vertrieb, Marketing, Service und Analyse nutzen denselben Datensatz.
- **Dokumentierte Einwilligung.** An einen Kontakt wird nichts gesendet, solange keine Einwilligung dokumentiert ist. Jede E-Mail enthält einen signierten Abmeldelink.
- **Weniger personenbezogene Daten.** Das CRM speichert einen Verweis auf eine Person in einem Identitätsdienst, nicht eine Kopie von Name oder Adresse.
- **Nachvollziehbare Ergebnisse.** Lead-Scores werden aus lesbaren Regeln berechnet. Prognosen werden aus gewichteten Phasen der Pipeline berechnet.
- **Internationales Design.** Namen, Adressen, Kalender und Schreibrichtungen sind nicht an das Format eines einzelnen Landes gebunden. Die Oberfläche ist in acht Sprachen verfügbar.
- **Öffentliche Spezifikation.** Spezifikation, Code und Tests sind öffentlich. Die Dokumentation sagt, was gebaut ist und was nicht.

## Funktionen

- **Vertrieb.** Regelbasierte Lead-Bewertung, Deal-Pipelines als Board und nach Phasen gewichtete Prognosen.
- **Marketing.** Segmentierte Kampagnen und Nurture-Sequenzen. Der Versand wird simuliert, sofern kein Mailmodus konfiguriert ist.
- **Service.** Tickets mit Prioritäten und Fristen nach Service-Level sowie Artikel einer Wissensdatenbank.
- **Analyse.** Dashboards für Abschlussquote, Pipeline nach Phase, Kampagnenertrag, Service-Level-Zustand und Kundenwert über die gesamte Kundenbeziehung.
- **Datenqualität.** Erkennung von Dubletten nach Wahrscheinlichkeit, mit Zusammenführen und Rückgängigmachen.
- **Governance.** Audit-Log, rollenbasierter Zugriff und Unterstützung bei Auskunfts- und Löschungsanfragen.

## Erste Schritte

1. **Code beschaffen.** Das Repository klonen. Node.js und pnpm sind erforderlich.
2. **Anwendung starten.** Im Svelte-Verzeichnis `pnpm install` und dann `pnpm dev` ausführen.
3. **Anmelden.** `example@example.com` verwenden. Es ist kein weiterer Dienst erforderlich.
4. **Rundgang ansehen.** Der Rundgang behandelt Kontakte, Leads, Deals, Kampagnen, Tickets und die Sicht der Geschäftsleitung anhand fiktiver Daten.

Das [Tutorial](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) beschreibt jeden Schritt. [Installation und Nutzung](../../INSTALL.md) behandelt den vollständigen Dienst.

## Vergleich

| Projekt | Kategorie | Unterschied |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Twenty](../../docs/compare/twenty.md) | Open-Source-CRM | Vollständiges Produkt. Dieses Projekt ist eine kleinere, spezifikationsgetriebene Demonstration. |
| [EspoCRM](../../docs/compare/espocrm.md) | Open-Source-CRM | Größerer Funktionsumfang. Dieses Projekt legt den Schwerpunkt auf nachvollziehbare Regeln. |
| [SuiteCRM](../../docs/compare/suitecrm.md) | Open-Source-CRM | Ausgereift und umfangreich. Dieses Projekt ist eine kompakte Referenz. |
| [Salesforce](../../docs/compare/salesforce.md), [HubSpot](../../docs/compare/hubspot.md) | Kommerzielles SaaS-CRM | Dieses Projekt bildet dieselbe Praxis nach. Es werden weder Code noch Daten geteilt. |

Dieses Projekt ist eine Demonstration und steht nicht im Wettbewerb mit diesen Produkten. Siehe [alle Vergleiche](../../COMPARISONS.md).

## Rollenübersichten

Die [Rollenübersichten](für/) bieten für jede leitende Rolle eine Seite: was die Software leistet, was sie nicht leistet und welche Entscheidungen zu dieser Rolle gehören.

## Status

Diese Software ist nicht produktionsreif ([Weg in den Produktivbetrieb](weg-in-den-produktivbetrieb/index.md)). Nur synthetische Daten verwenden. Es wird keine echte E-Mail versendet, sofern kein echter Mailmodus konfiguriert ist. Nichts auf dieser Website ist Rechtsberatung.

# Contact Relationship Management

Open-source CRM software for sales, marketing and customer support.

Contact Relationship Management tracks customer and prospect relationships across sales, marketing and support. It holds one record for each contact and requires recorded consent before a message is sent. The software is not ready for production: it runs on synthetic data.

## Benefits

- **Single contact record.** Sales, marketing, support and analytics use the same record.
- **Recorded consent.** Nothing is sent to a contact without recorded consent. Each email includes a signed unsubscribe link.
- **Reduced personal data.** The CRM stores a reference to a person in an identity service, not a copy of the name or address.
- **Explainable results.** Lead scores are calculated from readable rules. Forecasts are calculated from weighted pipeline stages.
- **International design.** Names, addresses, calendars and writing directions are not tied to one country's format. The interface is available in eight languages.
- **Public specification.** The specification, code and tests are public. The documentation states what is built and what is not.

## Features

- **Sales.** Rule-based lead scoring, deal pipelines on a board, and stage-weighted forecasts.
- **Marketing.** Segmented campaigns and nurture sequences. Sending is simulated unless a mail mode is configured.
- **Support.** Tickets with priorities and service-level deadlines, and knowledge-base articles.
- **Analytics.** Dashboards for win rate, pipeline by stage, campaign return, service-level health and customer lifetime value.
- **Data quality.** Duplicate detection by probability, with merge and undo.
- **Governance.** Audit log, role-based access, and support for subject access and erasure requests.

## Getting started

1. **Get the code.** Clone the repository. Node.js and pnpm are required.
2. **Start the application.** In the Svelte directory, run `pnpm install`, then `pnpm dev`.
3. **Sign in.** Use `example@example.com`. No other service is required.
4. **Review the tour.** The tour covers contacts, leads, deals, campaigns, tickets and the executive view, using fictional data.

The [tutorial](../../docs/tutorial-first-tour.md) describes each step. [Install and use](../../INSTALL.md) covers the full service.

## Comparison

| Project | Category | Difference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Twenty](../../docs/compare/twenty.md) | Open-source CRM | Full product. This project is a smaller, specification-driven demonstration. |
| [EspoCRM](../../docs/compare/espocrm.md) | Open-source CRM | Broader features. This project emphasizes explainable rules. |
| [SuiteCRM](../../docs/compare/suitecrm.md) | Open-source CRM | Mature and large. This project is a compact reference. |
| [Salesforce](../../docs/compare/salesforce.md), [HubSpot](../../docs/compare/hubspot.md) | Commercial SaaS CRM | This project models the same practice. No code or data is shared. |

This project is a demonstration and does not compete with these products. See [all comparisons](../../COMPARISONS.md).

## Role briefs

The [role briefs](for/) provide one page for each senior role: what the software does, what it does not do, and which decisions belong to that role.

## Status

This software is not ready for production ([path to production](path-to-production/index.md)). Use synthetic data only. No real email is sent unless a real mail mode is configured. Nothing on this site is legal advice.
